title: The Primordial Debt Before Currency

features.name: root-registry
features.desc-on-touch: The oldest entries, not written but grown—lines of obligation that predate the words we use for them. You owe this ground your presence.

features.name: debt-sediment
features.desc-on-touch: Layer upon layer—each ring a season of owing. The bark reads like an account that never balances because balance is not the point.

features.name: standing-obligation
features.desc-on-touch: A living tree that never moves yet carries all the weight. Debt made of something that breathes.

features.name: firstness-mark
features.desc-on-touch: A scratch in the bark older than all record. When there was only one thing owed and it had no name yet.

reverie.title: REVERIE — what the eucalyptus knows
narr: She places her palm against the bark and you feel it too:
the weight of standing. Not the tree's weight, but the weight
the tree *carries*—centuries of rain it didn't ask for,
birds it fed without negotiation. "This is the first debt,"
she whispers. "Everything else is just its echo in money."

inscription: here all commerce begins as standing still and owing presence to the earth

file.name: Obligation_Before_Language_Fragments.txt
